reason: Commit 3752851 delivered the remaining 24 development screens and the common monster-listening path. The boundary survey after it found three source-reachable appearance families without strict fresh evidence: named fruit, furniture, and M_AP_MONSTER. The preserved uncommitted candidate covers their apply.c and mhidden_description() bodies; validation now follows the source setup owners rather than narrowing the boundary or substituting a constructed state without authorization: makemon.c's runtime mimic appearance message for a directly created furniture mimic, and dogmove.c dog_eat()/quickmimic() for M_AP_MONSTER.

boundary.startingEvent: The hero applies a stethoscope and answers the direction prompt with an adjacent square: js/cmd.js dispatches `a` to doapply(), which reaches use_stethoscope() past confdir().
boundary.endingEvent: The top line C prints for that square, and the turn the listen does or does not spend. For an empty square that is "You hear nothing special." at apply.c:468; for a monster it is mstatusline()'s status line; for a mimic it is "That chest is really a small mimic." and then the status line.
boundary.validInputs: Any of the eight directions, plus the hero's own square, over every monster appearance the supported source build can produce. A Healer starts with an uncursed stethoscope at u_init.c:79. Ordinary generation, shipped special levels, dogmove.c quickmimic(), and wizard.c clonewiz() can all determine the adjacent monster's appearance before the listen begins.
boundary.observables: The top line and its --More-- redraws; the status line mstatusline() writes; gb.bhitpos and gn.notonhead; the free-versus-costly listen alternation already held in state.context.stethoscope_seq; and the vision map writes seemimic() and map_invisible() make. The arm consumes no randomness.
boundary.exclusions: Everything above confdir() at apply.c:379, which the port already refuses: a steed, an engulfer, a nonzero u.dz, and a cursed stethoscope. Below it: its_dead()'s statue arm, use_stethoscope()'s SDOOR and SCORR arms, and mstatusline()'s long-worm, u.ustuck and u.usteed arms, each of which needs setup no ported command reaches.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: apply.c use_stethoscope() (317-470) and its_dead() (196-309), read in full; insight.c mstatusline() (3273-3398) and size_str() (3202-3231); mon.c seemimic() (4406-4426); mkobj.c init_dummyobj() (3346-3371); objnam.c simple_typename() (296-307); invent.c nxtobj() (1477-1491).
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: The M_AP_TYPE switch at apply.c:404-437 over M_AP_OBJECT, M_AP_MONSTER and M_AP_FURNITURE; defsyms[].explanation and the generated CMAP_EXPLANATIONS projection; mstatusline()'s ordered info fragments; makemon.c syms[] and set_mimic_sym(); dogmove.c qm[]; wizard.c wizapp[]; and every shipped Lua appear_as descriptor under nethack-c/upstream/dat/.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Read from the C call graph of the two entry points. Already ported and needing no work: unmap_invisible(), newsym(), sobj_at(), can_reach_floor() (js/engrave.js, with the checkPit parameter), m_at(), find_mac, align_str, map_invisible(), obj_typename(), ustatusline(), mon_aligntyp(), rndmonnam(), set_mimic_sym() (js/makemon_create.js).
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: grep -rn '^seemimic' nethack-c/upstream/src/*.c returns only mon.c:4409, so js/mon.js's two 'display.c seemimic()' citations are wrong. grep -rn seemimic js/*.js returns six sites naming it as missing. grep -c Unsupported js/mhitu.js returns 0, so the giant bat's bites inside the stretch need nothing. grep -n explanation js/display.js returns nothing, so M_AP_FURNITURE needs a generated table. Re-run at 9657e3b while closing slice 1: `grep -rn "export function nxtobj" js/` and `grep -n "MZ_TINY" js/monsters.js` both return nothing, which is why apply.c:210-211's tiny-statue walk is refused rather than ported; js/monsters.js is generated by scripts/generate-monsters.mjs, so adding MZ_TINY is a generator change.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The boundary survey classified its_dead()'s excluded arms only to the depth needed to prove they stop before effects. Strict fresh cases now cover the common monster path, STRANGE_OBJECT, and visible-region mhidden_description(). A complete D:5 seed scan over 1..20000 found one adjacent named fruit whose level already diverges before the listen, and no adjacent furniture or monster disguise. A follow-up ordinary-level scan found furniture mimics at depths 15, 17, and 19 but not adjacent to arrival. Shipped Lua defines fixed furniture mimics in Rog-strt.lua and juiblex.lua; no shipped descriptor requests M_AP_MONSTER. Its source producers are dogmove.c quickmimic(), wizard.c clonewiz(), and arbitrary external Lua, so the first two supported-build routes are the remaining validation owners.

sourceReview: apply.c use_stethoscope() (317-470) and its_dead() (196-309) were read in full at 073cd13 against nethack-c/upstream, and every branch between confdir() at 379 and the return at 469 is entered above. Random-number order is unaffected: no arm inside the boundary draws, which is why the goal forecasts 33 screens and no change in the random-number total. Helpers were checked for existing ports one by one, and the four checks recorded in javascriptCrossCheck were run rather than assumed. Two limits stand: its_dead()'s corpse arm and mstatusline()'s info fragments are traced only to the depth that places them in later slices, and both are named in remainingLimits. Re-read at 9657e3b for slice 1: apply.c its_dead() (196-309) and use_stethoscope() (384-470) line by line, invent.c nxtobj() (1477-1491), trap.c uteetering_at_seen_pit() (6647-6653) and cmd.c:3346 sdir[]. The ported frame draws no random number, which both fresh differentials confirm: 1,813 and 2,701 calls, matching C exactly. Re-read at 022cd9a for slice 2: mon.c restrap() (4661-4693) and restore_cham() above it, mondata.h ceiling_hider() (43-45) and the is_hider, is_clinger and is_flyer macros it reads, monsters.h's eight M1_HIDE rows (675, 684, 694, 805, 814, 823, 986, 995), you.h:560 m_next2u(), display.h _sensemon() (55-58), trap.h:113 is_pit() and monst.h:73 M_AP_TYPE(). The guard's eight terms were traced in order against their positions in the random-number stream: rn2(3) is the fourth, so the three terms above it short-circuit with no draw and the four below it are reached only after the draw. m_next2u() was exported from js/mhitu.js rather than copied, because the duplicate-symbol report treats one C macro under two spellings as one defect.
